::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Feb 21st  1880  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester  
**Manuscript:** MS Lambeth Palace Library MS 2677 f.114
:::

Dear Madam

[Bishop Jenner](people/person_758.qmd) tells me that I should apply to you for permission to use two of [Dr Neale](people/person_1078.qmd)’s Songs of the Trades in a little [book of poetry](cmy_books/cmybook_143.qmd) for children which I am putting together for Marcus Ward  The Songs of the Engine Driver and the Silk Thrower are those that I mean, and I <u>may</u> perhaps also wish to have the Ironfounder, as well as the ballad of Aristomenes[^1] in the Greek history tales.  Hoping that you see no objection to my thus using them, I remain, 

yours respectfully
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: J. M. Neale, *Songs and Ballads for Manufacturers* (London: Burns 1846).   ‘Aristomenes and the Fox’ was published in J.M. Neale, *Stories from Heathen Mythology and Greek History for the Use of Christian Children* (London: Masters 1847).
